items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I’d been playing with Red Norvo for three years, with the quintet.

ctx.x: Oh it was over actually but I mean there was still remnants of stuff happening. And then there were a lot of records being made with bands with singers, with the singers featured instead of the band being featured. So as a matter of fact, when I eventually moved to

New York, I’d been playing with Red Norvo for three years, with the quintet. And we played all over. We played in Las Vegas a lot. We played for Frank Sinatra for his personal appearances for about a year and a half, and we played with Benny Goodman several times during that time, our first time to Europe. And everything, it was really like a great experience for me. Then when I did stay in New York, the work that I started to do mainly through — I knew Jerome Richardson from San Francisco and we had played…
That’s wonderful. So much of the music business is getting work through friends and establishing contacts.

items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: Jerry Dodgion,' so I got him and drummer and we opened in the Sands.

ctx.x: So I said, Pete would be great for it, so I wrote -- so we did it, so he was pleased and then he said what're you doing about Vegas, this year? I said, Gee, I don't know, I was supposed to go back in for Monte. He said, Well, I'm going in the Sands beginning in February, said call Monte.

So I called Monte, I said, 'You made any plans for me?' He said, 'See Red, I forgot, I haven't done it at all,' I said, 'Well, I got a chance to go another place,' I said for a month or two. He said, 'Go ahead.' So I said to Frank, 'I hate to do it with a trio, it's too hard in the lounges,' so he said, 'All right, add a couple of men.' So, I called Gene Wright, I said, 'Do you know anybody that's a cookin' anyplace I could (unintelligible) little saxophone player that plays good? He said, 'Yeah, I know, Jerry…
Now we opened there in February in the Lounge. He was -- Frank was in the big room. So, we stayed there until Labor Day.
